pack.title: Solarisael House craft starter
pack.description: A privacy-safe starter set of reusable engineering lessons from the House.

lessons.title: The spine: plain line, clean door, sharp refusal
lessons.lesson: Write the plain line. Leave one clean path through the system. Make every boundary state what it refuses.
lessons.trigger_context: Architecture, implementation, review, or any design with several competing paths.
lessons.proof_pattern: A reader can identify the main path, its boundary, and its rejected states without reconstructing hidden intent.

lessons.title: Make the first draft loud, then compress it
lessons.lesson: Use the long honest form until the real seam becomes visible. Compress only when the shorter form preserves the complete truth.
lessons.trigger_context: Early implementation, unclear boundaries, premature abstractions, or dense first drafts.
lessons.proof_pattern: The final form is shorter because one concept became clear, not because names or behavior disappeared.

lessons.title: A file should have one silhouette
lessons.lesson: Give each file one purpose. Every declaration in that file must support the same center of gravity.
lessons.trigger_context: Files that mix unrelated helpers, state, constants, classes, or runtime roles.
lessons.proof_pattern: Describe the file in one sentence. Split it when important contents do not fit that sentence.

lessons.title: A helper with a vague name exposes the wrong seam
lessons.lesson: Do not ship helpers named with helper, util, or several joined actions. Find the actual boundary and name that operation.
lessons.trigger_context: New helpers with vague names, several responsibilities, or names joined with and.
lessons.proof_pattern: The helper name identifies one operation and one boundary without generic suffixes or combined actions.

lessons.title: Refuse helpers that only launder anxiety
lessons.lesson: Remove wrappers that only rename a standard call or split a small coherent function. Keep helpers that own a real policy or boundary.
lessons.trigger_context: One-line wrappers, pass-through helpers, unnecessary indirection, or speculative organization.
lessons.proof_pattern: Removing the helper reduces indirection without duplicating policy, behavior, or error handling.

lessons.title: Count minimalism in concepts, not characters
lessons.lesson: Minimize abstractions, dependencies, and indirection. Do not remove plain names, useful spacing, or visible decisions to shorten the source.
lessons.trigger_context: Code golf, dense expressions, compressed diffs, or claims that fewer lines always mean simpler code.
lessons.proof_pattern: The chosen form requires fewer concepts from the next reader, even when it uses more lines.

lessons.title: Delete the clever line when the plain line reads better
lessons.lesson: Prefer visible control flow over dense expressions that require rereading. Compression must earn its cognitive cost.
lessons.trigger_context: Nested expressions, stacked comprehensions, chained transformations, or clever one-line control flow.
lessons.proof_pattern: A first-time reader can follow each decision once without decoding the expression backward.

lessons.title: Use negative space as punctuation
lessons.lesson: Place blank lines at completed thoughts and concern boundaries. Do not space by quota or remove every rest.
lessons.trigger_context: Cramped functions, noisy spacing, long loops, guard clauses, or formatting reviews.
lessons.proof_pattern: Each blank line marks a named transition. Each completed concern has enough space to remain visible.

lessons.title: Write documentation in simplified technical English
lessons.lesson: Use one idea per sentence, active voice, present tense, and one term per concept. Put each warning before its related instruction.
lessons.trigger_context: README files, procedures, deployment guides, operator instructions, and technical reference material.
lessons.proof_pattern: Procedural sentences stay under 20 words. Descriptive sentences stay under 25 words. Commands use the imperative form.

lessons.title: Explore existing behavior before rebuilding it
lessons.lesson: Inspect the working implementation and its tests before replacing a subsystem. Classify each behavior before designing the new seam.
lessons.trigger_context: Ports, adapters, rewrites, replacement runtimes, extractions, or new implementations of existing behavior.
lessons.proof_pattern: The change includes a behavior inventory with required, excluded, and superseded behavior before implementation begins.

lessons.title: Do not hard-code the current example to green
lessons.lesson: Fix the behavioral class instead of adding the latest names, phrases, identifiers, or paths to production logic.
lessons.trigger_context: A failing example suggests a new regex, exception, route, fixture, or special-case branch.
lessons.proof_pattern: Synthetic tests cover the failure shape. A differently worded equivalent input passes through the same structured mechanism.

lessons.title: Merge by intent before side
lessons.lesson: Do not choose ours, theirs, newest, or oldest by reflex. Name each intention and preserve every compatible invariant.
lessons.trigger_context: Merge conflicts, same-file overlap, collaborator synchronization, or branch promotion.
lessons.proof_pattern: The merge records both intentions, names surviving invariants, and verifies them in the integrated tree.

lessons.title: Branch promotion is not runtime proof
lessons.lesson: Treat commits, pushes, CI, deployment, and live behavior as separate facts. Prove each claimed stage independently.
lessons.trigger_context: Deployment, branch promotion, release checkpoints, or claims that work is live.
lessons.proof_pattern: Report the commit, remote ref, pipeline result, rollout state, and observable live behavior separately.

lessons.title: Verify cleanup and inspect the staged set
lessons.lesson: Confirm that temporary artifacts are gone. Inspect every staged path before committing instead of trusting a broad staging command.
lessons.trigger_context: Cleanup, temporary files, generated evidence, staging, commits, or cross-shell deletion.
lessons.proof_pattern: The temporary paths no longer exist. The staged set contains only required files in their correct locations.
